questions.question:
Identify the sentence that correctly uses inversion to emphasize the adverbial phrase.

A. Only after the rain stopped did the children return to the park.
B. Only after the rain stopped the children returned to the park.
C. Only after the rain stopped, the children returned to the park.
D. Only after the rain stopped were the children returning to the park.
options: Only after the rain stopped did the children return to the park.
Only after the rain stopped the children returned to the park.
Only after the rain stopped, the children returned to the park.
Only after the rain stopped were the children returning to the park.
questions.answer: Only after the rain stopped did the children return to the park.

questions.question:
Which of the following sentences correctly employs a cleft sentence to highlight the specific detail about the discovery?

A. It was in the library that the archaeologists found the ancient manuscript.
B. It was the library where the archaeologists found the ancient manuscript.
C. It was in the library that the archaeologists found the ancient manuscript.
D. It was in the library which the archaeologists found the ancient manuscript.
options: It was in the library that the archaeologists found the ancient manuscript.
It was the library where the archaeologists found the ancient manuscript.
It was in the library that the archaeologists found the ancient manuscript.
It was in the library which the archaeologists found the ancient manuscript.
questions.answer: It was in the library that the archaeologists found the ancient manuscript.

questions.question:
Select the correct form of the subjunctive mood required in the following sentence:

If only I _______ you that I was too unwell to attend the meeting yesterday.

A. knew
B. had known
C. would know
D. should know
options: knew
had known
would know
should know

questions.question:
Which option correctly uses ellipsis to maintain grammatical coherence in the following dialogue?

A. She said she would come, but she didn't.
B. She said she would come, but she not.
C. She said she would come, but she didn't come.
D. She said she would come, but she not coming.
options: She said she would come, but she didn't.
She said she would come, but she not.
She said she would come, but she didn't come.
She said she would come, but she not coming.
questions.answer: She said she would come, but she didn't.

questions.question:
Identify the sentence that appropriately uses formal register and complex sentence structure to convey a nuanced grammatical choice.

A. The committee decided not to approve the proposal because it lacked sufficient evidence.
B. The committee decided not to approve the proposal, lacking sufficient evidence.
C. The committee decided not to approve the proposal, for the reason that it lacked sufficient evidence.
D. The committee decided not to approve the proposal, which was because it lacked sufficient evidence.
options: The committee decided not to approve the proposal because it lacked sufficient evidence.
The committee decided not to approve the proposal, lacking sufficient evidence.
The committee decided not to approve the proposal, for the reason that it lacked sufficient evidence.
The committee decided not to approve the proposal, which was because it lacked sufficient evidence.
questions.answer: The committee decided not to approve the proposal, for the reason that it lacked sufficient evidence.
